title: Tenali Raman and the Astrologer's Broken Slate
summary: A pretentious court astrologer named Pandit Vidyadhar boasted before King Krishnadevaraya: 'Maharaj, with this astrological slate and chalk, I hold the past, present, and future...
full_text:
A pretentious court astrologer named Pandit Vidyadhar boasted before King Krishnadevaraya:
'Maharaj, with this astrological slate and chalk, I hold the past, present, and future of every soul in the palm of my hand!
No event occurs in this palace without my slate recording it beforehand!'

Tenali Raman walked into the council hall, holding his closed right hand behind his back.
Tenali bowed to the astrologer:
'Revered Pandit, since your slate records all events beforehand, write upon your slate right now:
What is currently held in my right hand behind my back?
Is it dead, or is it alive?'

The astrologer’s mind raced in a frantic dilemma:
If he wrote 'It is alive', Tenali could instantly squeeze his hand, kill the small sparrow or insect inside, and show it dead!
If he wrote 'It is dead', Tenali could simply open his hand and let the living creature fly away!
Believing he had discovered the trap, the astrologer wrote with a smug smile upon his slate:
**'It is in your own hands whether it lives or dies!'**

The astrologer showed the slate to the King, boasting: 'Behold my unassailable wisdom!'

Tenali Raman laughed with boundless amusement!
He brought his right hand out from behind his back, opened his fingers, and revealed:
Inside his palm was a common, small, polished round river pebble!

Tenali tapped the stone:
'Master Astrologer! A river pebble was never alive, nor can it ever die!
Your profound philosophical answer about living and dying was an evasive trick to cover your ignorance!
If your slate cannot tell the difference between a bird and a stone, how can you claim to guide the destiny of an empire?'

The entire court erupted in roaring laughter!
The astrologer dropped his chalk, hid his slate beneath his shawl, and shrank into the background.
King Krishnadevaraya smiled, acknowledging that Tenali’s simple stone had shattered a mountain of pretentious claims.
moral: Those who claim to read the secrets of heaven are blinded by the simplest earthly surprises.
